automations.name: New Lead Follow-Up
automations.summary: When someone submits the lead form on your website, this follows up right away by email and text, connects your office by phone if they don't reply, and checks in again the next day.

steps.title: Someone submits your website lead form
steps.body: The follow-up starts when someone submits the lead (intake) form on your website.
steps.note: All of these automations are still in Draft in GHL, so nothing is being sent yet. They'll go live once you approve. The trigger is set to your website lead form, but no form is selected yet, so it wouldn't fire. We'll connect it to the right form.

steps.title: The lead is added to your lead board
steps.body: They're added to the Marketing Pipeline as a New Lead.

steps.title: Email 1: Thanks for contacting us

email.subject: Thanks for claiming our offer [First name]!
email.body:
Thanks for claiming our [Promotion name] promotion [First name]!

We're looking forward to seeing you. Be sure to check out our calendar to schedule your appointment: [Booking link]

We also shot you a text if you have any questions in the meantime.

Hedayati Law Group, P.C.

steps.note: The subject talks about “claiming our offer”. If there's no offer, we suggest “Thanks for contacting Hedayati Law Group”.

steps.title: Text 1: Thanks for contacting us
steps.sms:
Hi [First name], thanks for claiming our [Promotion name] promotion - Have you worked with a lawyer on this issue in the past?

- Hedayati Law Group, P.C.
steps.note: This first text has no opt-out wording (“Reply STOP to opt out”), which carriers expect on the first message.

steps.when: If they reply and want to book
steps.gap: Waits up to 2 minutes for a reply
steps.title: Text 2: If they reply and want to book
steps.sms: Got it, so you know a little about what to expect. And just as a reminder: if you haven't already, be sure to schedule an appointment on our calendar here: [Booking link] You can also call us directly at [Office phone]
steps.body: When someone replies, they move to Hot Lead on your lead board. If their reply shows they want to book, they get this text.

steps.when: If they reply but aren't ready
steps.title: Text 2: If they reply but aren't ready to book
steps.sms: No problem. The next step is to book a time to come in - grab a spot that works for you here: [Booking link]

steps.when: If there's no reply after 2 minutes
steps.gap: If there's no reply after 2 minutes
steps.title: Your office is connected to the lead
steps.body: Your office phone rings with the message “A new lead has been generated. Their name is [Contact name]. Press any key to connect with [First name].” Pressing a key calls the lead.

steps.title: A recorded voicemail is left
steps.body: A pre-recorded voicemail is dropped on the lead's phone.
steps.note: We couldn't see a recording attached to this step. Please send us the voicemail you'd like to use, or we can help you record one.

steps.title: Text 3: Any questions?
steps.sms: Hi [First name], just checking back to see if you're ready to book an appointment so we can apply your discount. Are there any questions we can answer for you in the meantime? - Hedayati Law Group, P.C.
steps.note: This mentions “apply your discount”. If you don't offer a discount, we'll remove that part.

steps.title: The follow-up ends
steps.body: The lead leaves this automation.

questions.text: Is there an offer, such as a free consultation?
questions.why: The current texts and email mention a promotion and a discount, which came from a template.

questions.text: Who should get the call when a new lead doesn't reply?
questions.why: Right now the call goes to your main office line.

1 review request email, 1 review request text
Day 3, after your team is reminded

steps.title: A lead is marked Won

steps.note: All of these automations are still in Draft in GHL, so nothing is being sent yet. They'll go live once you approve.

steps.title: Any marketing follow-ups stop

steps.title: Review request email
steps.body: Your standard review request email is sent, with a link to leave a Google review.
steps.note: This uses the review request set up in GHL's Reputation settings. We'll add the exact wording here for you to review.

steps.title: Review request text
steps.body: Your standard review request text is sent, with a link to leave a Google review.
steps.note: This also uses the wording from your Reputation settings. We'll add it here for you to review.

steps.title: Your team is reminded to check for a review
steps.body: Everyone on your team gets an email: “Has [Contact name] left a review yet? If [Contact name] hasn't yet left a review, please follow up manually.”

steps.title: The review request ends

questions.text: When should a client be asked for a review?
questions.why: Today it's sent as soon as they're marked Won, which is often the day they hire you, before any work is done. Many firms wait until the matter is resolved.

questions.text: Who should get the 3-day review reminder?
questions.why: Right now it goes to every user in your account.

pipeline.name: Marketing Pipeline
pipeline.statusShort: Set up in GHL · automations in Draft
pipeline.status: These 7 stages already exist in your GHL account. The automations that move leads between them are built but still in Draft, so nothing moves on its own until you approve and we switch them on. Anything marked “Recommended” is a suggestion that hasn’t been set up.
pipeline.draftNote: All of these automations are still in Draft in GHL, so nothing is being sent and no leads are being moved yet. They go live once you approve them.

sectionText.overview: A quick summary of each automation we’ve built for you and how they connect, from the moment a lead contacts you to the review request after they hire you.
sectionText.pipeline: Your lead board in GHL. It shows each stage a lead moves through, what moves them, which moves are automatic, and where your team needs to step in.
sectionText.workflows: Exactly what starts each automation and what it does, step by step. Click any step to see the message, then mark it Looks good or Request a change.
sectionText.email: Every email in one place, so you can read the wording without opening each automation.
sectionText.sms: Every text message in one place, with the setup GHL needs before texts can be sent.
sectionText.approval: Everything we need from you before going live: your answers to our questions and your approval of each automation.

pipeline.diagramDesc: A website form puts a lead in New Lead. A reply moves them to Hot Lead and a booking moves them to New Booking. Your team then moves them to Visit Attended, Sale and Left a Review. Phone callers are added to Phone Lead by your team. No reply, missed consultations and 7 quiet days are handled by follow-ups and the Abandoned status. Marking a lead Won sends a review request.

stages.name: New Lead
stages.purpose: A new web enquiry you haven’t spoken to yet.
stages.entry: Submits the lead form on your website.
stages.next: Replies to the first text → Hot Lead. Books → New Booking. No reply → office call, voicemail and a next-day text.
stages.who: Your team takes the connect call when a new lead doesn’t reply. Who takes it is one of the questions in section 6.

stages.name: Phone Lead
stages.joinLabel: Team moves them when they book
stages.purpose: Someone who called you instead of filling in the form.
stages.entry: Your team adds them by hand.
stages.next: Your team moves them on once they book.
stages.automation: None. No follow-up messages are sent.
stages.recommend: Add callers automatically and send them the same follow-up as web leads. See section 6.

stages.name: Hot Lead
stages.purpose: The lead is engaged and talking to you.
stages.entry: Replies to the first follow-up text.
stages.next: Books → New Booking. 7 days with no activity → Abandoned.
stages.automation: New Lead Follow-Up (booking link text, or a short survey text if they aren’t ready)
stages.who: Your team replies to their messages in Conversations (to confirm).

stages.name: New Booking
stages.entry: Books a consultation on your calendar.
stages.next: Attends → your team moves them to Visit Attended. Misses it → reschedule email and texts.
stages.automation: Consultation Confirmation + Reminders, Missed Consultation Follow-Up
stages.flag: Before going live, we’ll connect these two automations to your “Schedule an Appointment” calendar. They currently point to a calendar that isn’t in your account.
stages.recommend: Move no-shows back to Hot Lead so it’s clear they still need a consultation. See section 6.

stages.name: Visit Attended
stages.entry: Your team moves them after the consultation.
stages.next: Hires you → Sale, and mark them Won. Doesn’t hire you → mark them Lost.
stages.recommend: Move leads here automatically when the appointment is marked “showed”. See section 6.

stages.name: Sale
stages.entry: Your team moves them when they sign up.
stages.next: Mark them Won to send the review request.
stages.automation: None from this stage. The review request runs when the lead is marked Won.
stages.recommend: Mark Won and move to Sale in one step. See section 6.

stages.name: Left a Review
stages.purpose: The client has left you a review. This is the last stage.
stages.entry: Your team moves them once the review appears.

outcomes.name: Closed Won
outcomes.label: Team marks Won
outcomes.purpose: How GHL records a new client.
outcomes.entry: Your team marks the lead Won.
outcomes.next: Marketing follow-ups stop, a review request goes out by email and text, and your team is reminded after 3 days.
outcomes.who: Your team marks Won. GHL does the rest.

outcomes.name: Closed Lost
outcomes.purpose: The lead won’t be hiring you, or has gone quiet.
outcomes.entry: Lost: your team marks it. Abandoned: no activity for 7 days in New Lead, Hot Lead or New Booking.
outcomes.who: Your team marks Lost. GHL marks Abandoned.
outcomes.recommend: Stop the Long-Term Nurture emails when a lead is marked Lost or Abandoned. See section 6.

stale.title: No activity for 7 days
stale.text: in New Lead, Hot Lead or New Booking → marked Abandoned automatically

ghlDoes: Adds web leads to New Lead and starts the follow-up
Moves a lead to Hot Lead when they reply to the first text
Rings your office if a new lead doesn’t reply within 2 minutes, then leaves a voicemail and sends a next-day text
Moves a lead to New Booking when they book, and stops the new-lead follow-up
Sends the confirmation and the 24-hour and 1-hour reminders
Sends reschedule messages after a missed consultation
Sends the review request when a lead is marked Won, and reminds your team after 3 days
Marks leads Abandoned after 7 days with no activity
teamDoes: Answers the connect call when a new lead doesn’t reply
Adds phone callers to Phone Lead
Moves leads to Visit Attended, Sale and Left a Review
Marks leads Won when they hire you, or Lost when they don’t
pipeline.teamNote: GHL doesn’t assign an owner to each lead, so these tasks fall to whoever on your team handles intake. Tell us if specific people should own them.

exceptions.today: Your office gets a connect call, the lead gets a voicemail and a next-day text, plus 4 weekly nurture emails. After 7 quiet days they’re marked Abandoned.
They get a reschedule email and text, and another text the next day if they don’t reply. They stay in New Booking.
exceptions.recommend: Move them back to Hot Lead.

exceptions.when: A lead goes quiet after replying or booking
exceptions.today: After 7 days with no activity they’re marked Abandoned, including leads with a consultation still coming up.
exceptions.recommend: Leave booked leads alone (question 2 of Stale Leads Clean-Up).

exceptions.when: A lead needs a personal follow-up
exceptions.today: No task or reminder is created. Follow-up depends on someone checking Conversations.
exceptions.recommend: Ask us if you’d like GHL to create a task for your team.

exceptions.when: A lead isn’t a fit, or decides not to hire you
exceptions.today: Your team marks them Lost. Nothing else happens, and the weekly nurture emails continue.
exceptions.recommend: Stop the nurture emails when a lead is marked Lost.

questions.text: How should people who phone your office get on the pipeline?
questions.why: Right now your team adds them to Phone Lead by hand, and they don’t get any follow-up messages.
options: Our team adds them by hand (as now)
Add them automatically and send the same follow-up as web leads (recommended)
We don’t need a Phone Lead stage

questions.text: When someone misses their consultation, where should they go?
questions.why: At the moment they stay in New Booking, so it looks like they still have a consultation coming up.
options: Move them back to Hot Lead (recommended)

questions.text: Should leads move to Visit Attended automatically?
questions.why: GHL can do this when the appointment is marked “showed” in the calendar.
options: No, our team will move them

questions.text: When someone hires you, what will your team do?
questions.why: The review request only goes out when a lead is marked Won. Moving them to Sale on its own doesn’t send it.
options: Mark them Won, and move them to Sale automatically (recommended)
Our team will do both by hand

questions.text: Should the weekly nurture emails stop when a lead is marked Lost or Abandoned?
questions.why: Today they keep going until all 4 have been sent.

questions.text: Do you want to review the Long-Term Nurture emails here too?
questions.why: New Lead Follow-Up adds every new lead to a 4-email nurture, one email a week. It’s built in GHL but isn’t on this page yet.

questions.text: Do these 7 stages match how your firm works?
questions.why: For example, you may want a stage for when a retainer or engagement letter has been sent but not signed.
options: We’d like to change them (use the request box in section 2)
